This is the first Act of the Parliament of India where "she/her" pronouns were used unlike the usual "he/him" pronouns.

Timeline

On 18 November 2022, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) announced the release of the Personal Data Protection (PDP) Bill, 2022 for public consultation. The Bill seeks to provide for the processing of personal data in a manner that recognizes the right of individuals to protect their personal data, the need to process personal data for lawful purposes and the need to balance the interests between the right of the individuals and the legitimate interests of the State, data controllers and data processors.

The Bill applies to the processing of personal data, where such processing is done in India or where such processing is done by a data fiduciary incorporated in India. The Bill categorizes personal data into sensitive personal data and critical personal data.

The Bill also introduces the concept of data localization, which requires certain categories of personal data to be stored only in India. The Bill also provides for the establishment of a Data Protection Authority of India (DPAI) to protect the interests of data principals, prevent misuse of personal data and ensure compliance with the provisions of the Bill.

In comparison to the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019, the PDP Bill, 2022 has made significant changes to the definition of personal data, the concept of data localization, and the powers and functions of the DPAI.

The PDP Bill, 2022 is a significant step towards ensuring the privacy and protection of personal data in India. It is expected to bring about greater transparency, accountability and fairness in the processing of personal data.
